name: argument-parser-negative-test-706c373f17/incorrect-named-arg-p.bal

spec_references.heading: Named and default arguments
spec_references.quote: Named arguments and omitted defaultable arguments are supported for function calls when the callee has an atomic function type with a known parameter signature.

reason: The source declares a public main function with one required int parameter and an empty body, which fits supported function definitions and required parameters. Its actual negative scenario is supplied by the harness comment: command-line input -j=1 names j although the entry point requires i. The specification covers named arguments in language function calls, but does not cover command-line argument parsing, entry-point argument binding, or rejection of unknown CLI parameter names. This whole case therefore depends on a not-covered runtime facility even though its Ballerina declaration is supported. There is no language call expression or invalid syntax to assess as a supported grammar rejection.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line named-argument parsing and rejection of an unknown entry-point parameter (-j=1).
test_design_notes: Mixed scope: supported required-parameter declaration with not-covered CLI behavior.

@args and @panic are harness comments, not language annotations. The panic marker expects invocation failure; no explicit panic occurs in the function body. No obvious syntax or migration corruption is visible.
